question.text: A point charge <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>–</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> is moved from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>S</mi></math> in a uniform electric field of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>30</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mrow><mo>–</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> directed along positive <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math>-axis. If coordinates of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>S</mi></math> are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mtext>and</mtext><mo> </mo><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> respectively, the work done by electric field will be

solution.text:
As electric field is uniform, so force acting on the charged particle will be uniform.

Therefore,

WE=F→·s→=qE→·s→

=2×10-230i^·0i^+0j^+0k^-i^+2j^+0k^

=-60×10-2 J

=-600 mJ
